clue.text: Pa needs braces adjusted and every typist knows it

indicators.note: letters that are adjusted are set in a new order, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Father's dental braces need fixing, a fact familiar to every typist in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' shuffles the letters of PA and BRACES together.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key along the bottom of a keyboard is used by every typist constantly, so they all know it.

clue.text: Come to a halt, whichever way you like

indicators.note: the entry reads identically forwards and backwards, so it can be read either way the solver likes

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Stop the car in any direction you fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whichever way you like' points out that the answer is a palindrome: it reads the same from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull up is a common phrasal verb for a driver or rider stopping.

clue.text: One taken in by more flexible wholesaler

indicators.note: one piece taken in by another sits inside it

parts.note: supple means flexible, so more flexible is suppler
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A trader is cheated by a wholesaler who bends the rules more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being cheated; here it puts I inside SUPPLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler sells goods on to retailers, which makes them a supplier of stock.

clue.text: Make the utmost effort in variety

definitions.meaning: to push oneself to the limit
a breed or type, as in a ... of wheat or virus

explanation.definitionFit: Strain is both a verb for exerting oneself hard and a noun for a particular breed or variety.

clue.text: Escape with policeman no longer in power

parts.note: a cop is slang for a policeman
a government voted out is no longer in power

explanation.surface: A fugitive gets away once the police chief has been removed from office.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop-out is an evasion, a way of escaping a duty or commitment.

clue.text: Intelligent but caught with jemmy

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a jemmy is a short crowbar, a kind of lever used by burglars

explanation.surface: A bright burglar who was nonetheless arrested holding a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever is a direct synonym of intelligent, describing quick mental ability.

clue.text: To be on the go is, maybe, subtle

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word could be arranged differently, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Being busy and active might be a subtle quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To bustle is to move about busily and energetically, which is being constantly on the go.

clue.text: Smooth stone turned over in more than one contest

parts.note: an even surface is smooth and level

indicators.note: turned over means the abbreviation is flipped to run backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A smooth pebble flipped over during several competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are competitions in a sports meeting, so the plural matches more than one contest.

clue.text: Intensive study leading to failure on the way

parts.note: a crash is a failure, as of a computer or market
a course is a route or way taken

explanation.surface: Cramming for an exam that ends in disaster along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading to' and 'on the' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash course is a short, intensive programme of instruction in a subject.

clue.text: Originally, Patsy Cline could have been a writer

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word
the letters could have been something else, signalling they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Country singer Patsy Cline might have chosen a writing career instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' gives P from Patsy; 'could have been' rearranges P with CLINE. Patsy Cline was an American country singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is an implement for writing, so in crossword terms it is a writer.

clue.text: Persistent decaying vegetable matter seen in the grass

indicators.note: something seen in another sits inside it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
peat is partly decayed plant matter found in bogs

explanation.surface: Rotting plant matter keeps turning up in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal; 'the' before grass is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeated happens again and again, so it is persistent or recurring.

clue.text: Basil, perhaps, is exposed by Father Brown

indicators.note: the letters are exposed by being visible across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone called Basil has his secret revealed by G K Chesterton's priest detective.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Father Brown', the fictional priest detective. 'Basil' looks like a man's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary plant used for flavouring, an example of a herb, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Asian poets might be emotional

indicators.note: the letters might be something else, signalling they should be rearranged

explanation.surface: Poets from Asia may well be given to strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate describes someone showing strong feelings, a close synonym of emotional.

clue.text: Part of the theatre treat — going to "The Ring"

parts.note: to dress a wound is to treat it
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A night out at the theatre to see a production of Wagner's Ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' only joins the pieces; 'The Ring' suggests Wagner's opera cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress circle is the first tier of seating above the stalls in a theatre.

clue.text: Boy embraces woman in black to get going

indicators.note: one word embracing another holds it inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
a witch is traditionally pictured as a woman dressed in black

explanation.surface: A lad hugs a woman dressed in mourning before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' is the container signal: the boy holds the woman in black.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch on a machine is to start it up, to get it going.

clue.text: Author and wife about to break a long spear

indicators.note: one piece breaks another by splitting it open

parts.note: a lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A writer and his wife are on the verge of snapping a lengthy weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' is the container signal. D H Lawrence wrote Sons and Lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: D H Lawrence was an English novelist, and T E Lawrence also wrote, so the surname names an author.

clue.text: Warning to vacate compound

indicators.note: to compound is to mix ingredients together, so the letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A notice tells people to leave the walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a noun for an enclosure but signals mixing up VACATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary note or warning, from Latin 'let him beware'.

clue.text: Honour card promoted in raise

parts.note: the jack is one of the honour cards in bridge
someone promoted has gone up

explanation.surface: A knave of trumps advanced during a bidding raise at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack up is to lift with a jack, or to increase prices, so it means to raise.

clue.text: Stay with baby almost to the end

parts.note: to last is to stay or endure
baby as an adjective means tiny, which is minute

explanation.surface: Remaining with an infant until nearly the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Last-minute describes something done at the latest possible moment, right up close to the deadline.

clue.text: Free sample found in Queer Street

indicators.note: queer in its old sense of odd signals the letters are set strangely

explanation.surface: A complimentary sample discovered in a state of financial trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queer Street' is an old British phrase for debt or difficulty; here 'Queer' rearranges STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is a small sample of a product, such as perfume, offered free to try.

clue.text: England takes a long time to win

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: England's team takes ages to secure victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone's attention or affection is to attract and win it over.

clue.text: Women's punishment, having stole

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to take the rap is to accept punishment

explanation.surface: A woman is punished for having stolen something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a verb but is the noun, a shawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap is a shawl or scarf worn over the shoulders, the same garment as a stole.

clue.text: Footballer accepts order for keeping feet warm

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside

parts.note: Becks is the nickname of English footballer David Beckham
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order

explanation.surface: A football star receives an honour for his services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' is the container signal; 'Footballer' is the nickname of David Beckham, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedsocks are thick socks worn in bed, whose purpose is keeping feet warm at night.

clue.text: Europeans wanting end of disgusting smells

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: reeks means smells strongly and unpleasantly

explanation.surface: Continental visitors wanting to get rid of revolting odours.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeks are the people of Greece, a European country, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: Time taken by Spartan serf to get everything

parts.note: a helot was a serf in ancient Sparta

explanation.surface: An ancient Spartan slave seizes time to acquire all he can.
explanation.definitionFit: The lot is an informal phrase meaning the whole amount, everything.

clue.text: Good or bad chap has wine-based drink in small container

parts.note: a man can be called a good egg or a bad egg
a cup is a punch-like drink often made with wine, as in claret cup

explanation.surface: A fellow of some sort enjoys a glass of wine punch in a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An eggcup is a small holder for a boiled egg at the table.
